claims.claim: Across forty DAOs in eight segments the unweighted dataset mean is 67.3 of 130 points (51.8 percent): the median DAO has implemented roughly half of the institutional architecture the framework prescribes.
conditions: forty operational DAOs against the thirteen-category rubric
claims.source: The Institutional Deficit in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations - An Empirical Analysis
claims.quote: The unweighted dataset mean total of 67.3 of 130 (51.8 percent) is the central quantitative finding: the median DAO has implemented roughly half of what the framework prescribes.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Institutional Deficit in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations - An Empirical Analysis (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6819121

claims.claim: The institutional deficit is structural rather than incidental: DAO architecture has solved decentralized capital formation and programmable value transfer, and has not yet solved AI-mediated governance, Sybil-resistant identity, and constitutional separation of powers.
conditions: forty operational DAOs against the thirteen-category rubric
claims.source: The Institutional Deficit in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations - An Empirical Analysis
claims.quote: The deficit is structural rather than incidental. It reflects that DAO architecture has solved the problems for which it was originally designed, decentralized capital formation and programmable value transfer, and has not yet solved the problems that emerged after its design
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Institutional Deficit in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations - An Empirical Analysis (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6819121

claims.claim: A visibility paradox holds across every segment: categories producing visible artifacts score consistently above the midpoint while categories producing invisible governance infrastructure score consistently below it.
conditions: forty operational DAOs against the thirteen-category rubric
claims.source: The Institutional Deficit in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations - An Empirical Analysis
claims.quote: Categories that produce visible artifacts, token launches, treasury balances, mission statements, marketplace activity, contract automation, score consistently above 5 across the dataset. Categories that produce invisible institutional infrastructure, legal wrappers, judicial branches, AI alignment policies, on-chain reputation ledgers, agent-identity protocols, score consistently below 5.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Institutional Deficit in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations - An Empirical Analysis (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6819121

claims.claim: Investment in invisible institutions is systematically underprovided relative to investment in visible institutions, even when the invisible institutions are more important to long-run resilience.
conditions: institutional investment incentives under the visibility paradox
claims.source: The Institutional Deficit in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations - An Empirical Analysis
claims.quote: Investment in invisible institutions is therefore systematically underprovided relative to investment in visible institutions, even when the invisible institutions are more important to long-run resilience.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Institutional Deficit in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations - An Empirical Analysis (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6819121

claims.claim: A DAO can be highly successful on visible categories and effectively non-functional on invisible categories simultaneously, as ConstitutionDAO's maximum Fundraising score paired with minimum Governance score shows.
conditions: ConstitutionDAO as the dataset's extreme visibility-paradox case
claims.source: The Institutional Deficit in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations - An Empirical Analysis
claims.quote: A DAO can be highly successful on visible categories and effectively non-functional on invisible categories simultaneously.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Institutional Deficit in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations - An Empirical Analysis (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6819121

claims.claim: Market discipline alone will not produce balanced institutional development, because it under-invests in the invisible institutional infrastructure that is most predictive of long-run resilience.
conditions: the public-goods argument applied to the DAO sector
claims.source: The Institutional Deficit in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations - An Empirical Analysis
claims.quote: the visibility paradox implies that market discipline alone will not produce balanced institutional development. Market discipline produces under-investment in invisible institutional infrastructure, and the institutional infrastructure that is most predictive of long-run resilience is precisely the institutional infrastructure that is most underprovided.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Institutional Deficit in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations - An Empirical Analysis (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6819121
